(3) func_ov002_020dc560 (ordinal 487) already byte-matched; it had no `complete` marker. Folded, it is verified like every other member, including tools/reloc_audit.py check_destinations(), which is the check the superseded entry asked for before enrolling it. It calls func_01ff99a4 and func_01ff98f4, two interior entry points of the soft-float routine src/unnamed/arm9/01ff/func_01ff97d8.c, which is one enrolled hand-asm block spanning 0x01ff97d8..0x01ffa344. mwccarm 2004/b56 cannot export a second symbol from one asm block (measured and recorded in config/rombuild-exclude.txt for func_01ffa440), and that block cannot be split at those addresses: 36 of its branches cross 0x01ff98f4, 0x01ff99a4, 0x01ff9d40 or 0x01ff9e2c into shared exception tails. So no object defines the two names; tools/lcf_interior.py, run by rombuild.py and by tubuild.py linkcheck, adds `func_01ff98f4 = 0x01ff98f4;` and `func_01ff99a4 = 0x01ff99a4;` to the linker command file because daPly_c.o imports them and nothing defines them, and the calls resolve to those absolute definitions (ITCM never moves, so the symbols.txt address is the linked address). An earlier revision of this fold stopped at 0x020dc560 for want of exactly those two symbols. EDGE 1 stops at 0x020e67a8 and not at the run end 0x020e6a08 because the last five functions of the run are the destructor tail: daPly_c D0 (0x020e67a8), D1 (0x020e6858), C1 (0x020e68f4), daPly_c::OnYoshiTryEat (0x020e69b8) and func_ov002_020e69c0. The cartridge orders D0 below D1, the order mwccarm gives an INLINE destructor that something forces out of line; include/daPly_c.h declares `virtual ~daPly_c();` out of line and it is the key function, so defining it here would make this TU emit _ZTV7daPly_c and daPly_c's RTTI and would need a header edit that reaches all of its consumers. Those five stay one-function sources; a later widening that solves the destructor can take them and the vtable together. Same original TU, not a boundary: the fold makes no claim that 0x020e67a8 is where the original file ended.

DESTRUCTOR TAIL (EDGE 1 moved up from 0x020e67a8 to the run end 0x020e6a08) and the static initializer. Measured on 2004/b56 before the splice: an out-of-line daPly_c::~daPly_c() {} emits three .text sections in order D2 (0x9c), D0 (0xb0), D1 (0x9c), plus _ZTV7daPly_c and _ZTI7daPly_c/_ZTS7daPly_c. The cartridge has no D2. While the class was spelled Player its RTTI had no cartridge home (the vtable's typeinfo word at 0x0210a838 relocates to _ZTI7daPly_c, 0x0210a56c, whose name string is 7daPly_c), so the definition was compiled under #pragma RTTI off; since the rename to the cartridge spelling the pragma is gone and _ZTI7daPly_c/_ZTS7daPly_c are compared as deadstrip-data. Under #pragma defer_codegen off the variants come out D1, D0, D2; defer_codegen is on for this definition only, which emits D2, D0, D1, and it is turned back off before C1. D2 is deadstripped. _ZTV7daPly_c (0x84, preamble plus 31 slots) is owned .data at ov002:0x0210a83c, storage 0x0210a834: the 124 slot bytes match and this TU's copy is the linked one. D0 and D1 bytes and relocations match the enrolled bodies. C1 and OnYoshiTryEat are the enrolled bodies. func_ov002_020e69c0 keeps its C bytes with a void* parameter so it agrees with the call in this file. __sinit_ov002_021019d0 is the enrolled C body under #pragma cplusplus off, placed in .init by #pragma define_section; a standalone compile of that wrapping is byte-identical and relocation-identical to the .c object (0x5470, 1841 relocs) with and without #pragma defer_codegen off. This job is the sanctioned exception to the fold-worker Skip daPly_c rule and to the pool exclusion of ov002_021019d0.

Written by hand, not by tools/tubuild.py create: at the time of writing, create() raised AttributeError in build_manifest_entry the moment a member of the run had no legacy source, and this run has three such members; it also wrote the .cpp before crashing, so its output could not be trusted as a starting point. That defect has SINCE BEEN FIXED on main (#2315 makes create survive a sourceless member, #2323 makes it emit an // @symbol marker per member), so a future entry for this module need not be hand-written. The builder audited all 301 hand-written rows against the pre-promotion tree: ordinals contiguous 0..300, rows tile 0x020bd828..0x020cfea4 with no gap or overlap, and every legacy_source is both a file in the base tree and an exact-path entry in the base ov002 delinks.txt with the matching extension (173 .cpp, 128 .c).

The source was assembled by a scoped generator that reuses tubuild's own split_legacy_source/unit_functions, because create()'s preamble merge does not scale to 301 members: it emits one merged file-scope declaration per ROM symbol, and 301 independent recoveries of one symbol disagree constantly. Measured instead, and used here: in mwccarm 2004/b56 a declaration written at BLOCK scope inside an `extern "C"` region gets C linkage, and two function bodies may declare one C symbol with different types. So every member keeps its own declarations inside its own body and no call site had to be rewritten to fit a merged spelling. The same is true of DATA declarations -- measured directly, contradicting the earlier belief that block-scope data redeclaration is rejected; only a file-scope redeclaration is. That matters for bytes, not just for tidiness: hoisting one canonical data declaration and casting each member's view back with a macro changed the codegen of six members, and the choice of which spelling became canonical depended on which other members were present.

Only what a function body cannot hold is hoisted: a namespace, a class with static or declared-but-undefined members, and any type named in a member's own signature. Those tags are made unique per member. `struct Sound` and `namespace Sound` were the one true conflict and were resolved to the namespace spelling, which mangles identically.

PRAGMA, measured with the delete-outright control first, and RE-MEASURED by the builder at the shipped revision -- the writer's counts predate the three near-miss recoveries in this branch and no longer reproduce. The shard for ordinal 35, _ZN7daPly_c7SetAnimEji5Fix12IiEj, carries `#pragma opt_propagation off`. Under default deferred codegen that pragma is FILE-GLOBAL: it costs 46 other members their match (255/301 with it file-global, 300/301 with it simply deleted). Bracketing it in #pragma push/pop buys back nothing at all -- also 300/301, byte-identical to deleting it -- because with codegen deferred the state that binds is the state at end of file. `#pragma defer_codegen off` plus a ROM-ASCENDING source order makes the bracket bind positionally and recovers ordinal 35 as well: 301/301, which is what this entry's verification block records. Deleting only `defer_codegen off` still scores 300/301 on bytes, but the emitted .text order reverses (300 out-of-order ordinal pairs) and the pre-link object audit refuses with `licensed .text functions are not emitted in ROM address order`; the byte compare alone would not have caught it. That is why this file is written low address first, the opposite of the default deferred-codegen convention.

Two members needed a source change to survive the C-to-C++ language flip, both the same construct and both from the known scalarization family: a two-int struct copy (`*(Pair2i *)dst = *(Pair2i *)(p + k)`) that C compiles as load/load/store/store and C++ scalarizes into load/store/load/store. The array-wrapper view (`struct P2w { int w[2]; }; *(P2w *)dst = *(P2w *)(p + k);`) restores the ROM's shape exactly, in func_ov002_020c14b8 and func_ov002_020c25a8. Three other spellings were measured and rejected first (two scalar locals: 4 words wrong; copy through a named temporary: 12 bytes too long). The builder diffed all 301 shipped bodies against their pre-promotion shards and found a SECOND change family this note omitted: func_ov002_020c6fe4 and func_ov002_020c897c each do arithmetic on a `void **` load, `*(void**)(c + id*4 + 0xdc) + 0x50`, which is a GNU extension C accepts under -gccext and C++ does not; both casts became `char **`. Byte-neutral -- the address arithmetic is identical -- but an edit. Apart from those four members and the local struct TAG renames that hoisting forces (Vector3 -> Vec3i, V3 -> V3a/V3b, Obj -> ObjHS and Obj2fec, State -> State3i, Camera -> CameraRaw), no body was rewritten.
All 301 members reproduce the cartridge byte-for-byte; none is NONMATCHING and none carries an asm body.
